title: Penalty and compensation for damage to computer, computer system
summary: If a person, without permission of the owner, accesses a computer, downloads or copies data, introduces a virus, damages data, disrupts a system, or denies access to an authorised user, they are liable to pay compensation to the affected person.
punishment: Compensation to the affected person (civil liability).

title: Tampering with computer source documents
summary: Knowingly or intentionally concealing, destroying, or altering computer source code that is required to be kept by law.
punishment: Imprisonment up to 3 years, or fine up to Rs 2 lakh, or both.

title: Computer related offences (hacking)
summary: If any person dishonestly or fraudulently does any act referred to in Section 43 (unauthorised access, data theft, damage, etc.), it is a punishable offence.
punishment: Imprisonment up to 3 years, or fine up to Rs 5 lakh, or both.

title: Identity theft
summary: Fraudulently or dishonestly using the electronic signature, password, or any other unique identification feature of another person.
punishment: Imprisonment up to 3 years and fine up to Rs 1 lakh.

title: Cheating by personation using computer resource
summary: Cheating by pretending to be someone else using a computer resource or communication device — covers phishing, fake profiles, UPI/online payment fraud, and impersonation scams.
punishment: Imprisonment up to 3 years and fine up to Rs 1 lakh.

title: Violation of privacy
summary: Intentionally capturing, publishing, or transmitting the image of a private area of a person without consent, violating their privacy.
punishment: Imprisonment up to 3 years, or fine up to Rs 2 lakh, or both.

title: Cyber terrorism
summary: Acts intended to threaten the unity, integrity, security, or sovereignty of India by denying access to a computer resource, unauthorised access to a protected system, or introducing contaminants — likely to cause death, injury, or damage to critical infrastructure.
punishment: Imprisonment which may extend to imprisonment for life.

title: Publishing or transmitting obscene material in electronic form
summary: Publishing or transmitting, in electronic form, material that is lascivious or appeals to prurient interest.
punishment: First conviction: up to 3 years and fine up to Rs 5 lakh. Subsequent: up to 5 years and fine up to Rs 10 lakh.

title: Child sexually explicit material (CSAM)
summary: Publishing, transmitting, creating, collecting, or browsing material depicting children in sexually explicit acts in electronic form.
punishment: First conviction: up to 5 years and fine up to Rs 10 lakh. Subsequent: up to 7 years and fine up to Rs 10 lakh.

title: Breach of confidentiality and privacy
summary: A person who, having secured access to electronic records or information under powers of the Act, discloses it to another person without consent.
punishment: Imprisonment up to 2 years, or fine up to Rs 1 lakh, or both.

title: Punishment for murder
summary: Whoever commits murder shall be punished. Murder is causing death with the intention of causing death or bodily injury sufficient to cause death.
punishment: Death, or imprisonment for life, and fine.

title: Attempt to murder
summary: Doing an act with the intention or knowledge that, if it caused death, would amount to murder.
punishment: Imprisonment up to 10 years and fine; if hurt is caused, may extend to life imprisonment.

title: Voluntarily causing hurt
summary: Punishment for voluntarily causing hurt to another person.
punishment: Imprisonment up to 1 year, or fine up to Rs 1,000, or both.

title: Stalking
summary: Following a woman and contacting or attempting to contact her despite disinterest, or monitoring her use of the internet, email, or any electronic communication (cyber-stalking).
punishment: First conviction: up to 3 years; subsequent: up to 5 years; and fine.

title: Punishment for theft
summary: Dishonestly taking movable property out of the possession of a person without their consent.
punishment: Imprisonment up to 3 years, or fine, or both.

title: Punishment for robbery
summary: Theft is robbery if the offender voluntarily causes or attempts to cause death, hurt, or wrongful restraint or fear thereof in order to commit the theft.
punishment: Rigorous imprisonment up to 10 years and fine.

title: Criminal breach of trust
summary: Dishonestly misappropriating or converting to one's own use property that was entrusted to them.
punishment: Imprisonment up to 3 years, or fine, or both.

title: Cheating and dishonestly inducing delivery of property
summary: Cheating someone and thereby dishonestly inducing them to deliver property or to make, alter, or destroy a valuable security. Commonly applied to fraud and online scams alongside IT Act sections.
punishment: Imprisonment up to 7 years and fine.

title: Punishment for forgery
summary: Making a false document or electronic record with intent to cause damage or injury, or to commit fraud.
punishment: Imprisonment up to 2 years, or fine, or both.

title: Defamation
summary: Making or publishing any imputation concerning a person intending to harm their reputation, including online posts. Section 500 prescribes the punishment.
punishment: Simple imprisonment up to 2 years, or fine, or both.

title: Criminal intimidation
summary: Threatening another person with injury to their person, reputation, or property, with intent to cause alarm — includes threats made online or by message.
punishment: Imprisonment up to 2 years, or fine, or both; up to 7 years if the threat is to cause death or grievous hurt.

title: Word, gesture or act intended to insult the modesty of a woman
summary: Uttering any word, making any sound or gesture, or exhibiting any object intending to insult the modesty of a woman, or intruding upon her privacy — includes obscene online messages.
punishment: Simple imprisonment up to 3 years and fine.

title: Information in cognizable cases (FIR)
summary: Every information relating to the commission of a cognizable offence given to an officer in charge of a police station must be reduced to writing, read over to the informant, signed, and recorded in the prescribed form — this is the First Information Report (FIR). A copy is given to the informant free of cost.
punishment: Procedural — governs registration of an FIR.

title: When police may arrest without warrant
summary: Specifies the circumstances in which a police officer may arrest a person without an order from a Magistrate and without a warrant, primarily for cognizable offences.
punishment: Procedural — governs arrest powers.

title: Examination of witnesses by police
summary: Empowers an investigating police officer to examine orally any person supposed to be acquainted with the facts and circumstances of the case, and to reduce statements to writing.
punishment: Procedural — governs witness examination during investigation.
